# proc

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/pkg/proc"
```

Package proc runs supervised processes.

A process is a struct that embeds im.Process and has a Run\(context.Context\) method with a pointer receiver. Start creates the process from its zero value, runs Run in a new goroutine, and returns a Ref. Callers keep the Ref and call exported methods directly on the result of Ref.Get. The immutago analyzer proves that these methods take and return only immutable values and Refs.

A supervisor runs its children until Stop. If Run returns, the process ends. If Run panics, the supervisor runs it again on the same value after a delay of 1 s that doubles for each restart in the last 5 minutes. A sixth panic in 5 minutes stops all children of the supervisor in reverse start order and escalates the panic to the parent supervisor, which restarts the subtree with the same rule. At the root supervisor, the escalation panics again with the last panic value, and the program exits.

## type Ref

Ref refers to a process that Start created.

```go
type Ref[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Start

```go
func Start[T any, P interface {
    *T
    Run(context.Context)
}](parent *Supervisor) Ref[T]
```

Start creates a T from its zero value and runs its Run method under parent. If parent is stopped, Start returns the Ref and does not run the process.

### func \(Ref\[T\]\) Get

```go
func (r Ref[T]) Get() *T
```

Get returns the process with one atomic load.

## type Supervisor

Supervisor runs processes and nested supervisors.

```go
type Supervisor struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func New

```go
func New() *Supervisor
```

New returns a root supervisor.

### func \(\*Supervisor\) Stop

```go
func (s *Supervisor) Stop() <-chan struct{}
```

Stop stops the children of s in reverse start order and does not wait. The returned channel closes when all children have stopped. A process can stop its own supervisor from Run.

### func \(\*Supervisor\) Supervise

```go
func (s *Supervisor) Supervise() *Supervisor
```

Supervise returns a new supervisor that s runs as a child.
